questions.stem:
The following diagram shows a circle with centre O and radius $4\text{ cm}$.

**diagram not to scale**

![Circle with centre O and radius 4. The shaded sector POR has angle θ at O; Q lies on the arc between P and R.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q1.png)

The points P, Q and R lie on the circumference of the circle and $\text{P}\hat{\text{O}}\text{R} = \theta$, where $\theta$ is measured in radians.

The length of arc PQR is $10\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the perimeter of the shaded sector.
parts.markscheme:
attempts to find perimeter ***(M1)***

arc $+ 2 \times$ radius OR $10 + 4 + 4$

$= 18$ (cm) ***A1***

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the shaded sector.

questions.stem: A function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x - 2}$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $x \neq 2$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has a vertical asymptote and a horizontal asymptote.

Write down the equation of

(i) the vertical asymptote;

(ii) the horizontal asymptote.

parts.label: b
c
parts.text:
On the following set of axes, sketch the graph of $y = f(x)$, showing all the features found in parts (a) and (b).

![Empty grid with x and y axes from −5 to 5.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q3-axes.png)
parts.markscheme:
![Sketch of y = 1 − 1 divided by (x − 2): two branches, asymptotes x = 2 and y = 1, intercepts (0, 1.5) and (3, 0).](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q3c-ms.png)

two correct branches with correct asymptotic behaviour and intercepts clearly shown ***A1***

questions.stem:
The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ by

$$f(x) = ax + b, \text{ where } a,\ b \in \mathbb{Z}$$

$$g(x) = x^2 + x + 3.$$

parts.text: Find the two possible functions $f$ such that $(g \circ f)(x) = 4x^2 - 14x + 15$.
parts.markscheme:
attempts to form $(g \circ f)(x)$ ***(M1)***

$[f(x)]^2 + f(x) + 3$ OR $(ax + b)^2 + ax + b + 3$

$a^2x^2 + 2abx + b^2 + ax + b + 3 \ \left(= 4x^2 - 14x + 15\right)$ ***(A1)***

equates their corresponding terms to form at least one equation ***(M1)***

$a^2x^2 = 4x^2$ OR $a^2 = 4$ OR $2abx + ax = -14x$ OR $2ab + a = -14$ OR $b^2 + b + 3 = 15$

$a = \pm 2$ (seen anywhere) ***A1***

attempt to use $2ab + a = -14$ to pair the correct values (seen anywhere) ***(M1)***

$f(x) = 2x - 4$ (accept $a = 2$ with $b = -4$), $f(x) = -2x + 3$ (accept $a = -2$ with $b = 3$) ***A1A1***

questions.stem:
The following diagram shows part of the graph of a quadratic function $f$.

The vertex of the parabola is $(-2,\ -5)$ and the $y$-intercept is at point P.

![Upward parabola f with vertex (−2, −5), crossing the y-axis at P below the x-axis.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q7a.png)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the equation of the axis of symmetry.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The function can be written in the form $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}(x - h)^2 + k$, where $h,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}$.
parts.text: Write down the values of $h$ and $k$.

parts.label: d
parts.intro:
In the following diagram, the line $L$ is normal to the graph of $f$ at point P.

![The parabola f with the line L through P, normal to f at P; L meets f again at Q in the second quadrant.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q7b.png)
parts.text: Find the equation of the line $L$, in the form $y = ax + b$.
parts.markscheme:
$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}(x + 2) \ \left(= \dfrac{1}{2}x + 1\right)$ ***(A1)***

substituting $x = 0$ into their derivative ***(M1)***

$f'(0) = 1$

gradient of normal is $-1$ (may be seen in their equation) ***A1***

$y = -x - 4$ (accept $a = -1$, $b = -4$) ***A1***

> **Note:** Award ***A0*** for $L = -x - 4$ (without the $y =$).

parts.label: e
parts.intro: The line $L$ intersects the graph of $f$ at a second point, Q, as shown above.
parts.text: Calculate the distance between P and Q.
parts.markscheme:
equating their $f(x)$ to their $L$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1}{4}(x + 2)^2 - 5 = -x - 4$

$\dfrac{1}{4}x^2 + 2x = 0$ (or equivalent) ***(A1)***

valid attempt to solve their quadratic ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1}{4}x(x + 8) = 0$ OR $x(x + 8) = 0$

$x = -8$ ***A1***

> **Note:** Accept both solutions $x = -8$ and $x = 0$ here, $x = -8$ may be seen in working to find coordinates of Q or distance.

substituting their value of $x$ (not $x = 0$) into their $f(x)$ or their $L$ ***(M1)***

$y = -(-8) - 4$ or $y = \dfrac{1}{4}(-8 + 2)^2 - 5$

$\text{Q}(-8,\ 4)$ ***A1***

correct substitution into distance formula ***(A1)***

$\sqrt{(-8 - 0)^2 + (4 - (-4))^2}$

distance $= \sqrt{128} \ \left(= 8\sqrt{2}\right)$ ***A1***

questions.stem: Consider an acute angle $\theta$ such that $\cos\theta = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
(i) attempt to use Pythagoras ***(M1)***

$\sin^2\theta + \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 = 1$ OR $x^2 + 2^2 = 3^2$ OR right triangle with side $2$ and hypotenuse $3$

$\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ ***A1***

(ii) attempt to substitute into double-angle identity using their value of $\sin\theta$ ***(M1)***

$\sin 2\theta = 2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$\sin 2\theta = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.intro:
The following diagram shows triangle ABC, with $\hat{\text{B}} = \theta$, $\hat{\text{A}} = 2\theta$, $\text{BC} = a$ and $\text{AC} = b$.

![Triangle ABC with angle θ at B, angle 2θ at A, side BC = a and side AC = b.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q8a.png)
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1 (using values from part (a))**

$\dfrac{b}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{a}{\sin 2\theta}$

attempt to use sine rule with their values from part (a) ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{b}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)} = \dfrac{a}{\left(\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}\right)}$ OR $\dfrac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)}{b} = \dfrac{\left(\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}\right)}{a}$

correct working that leads to ***AG*** ***A1***

$\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}a = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}b$ OR $\dfrac{3b}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{9a}{4\sqrt{5}}$ OR $\dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{4b}{9}$ (or equivalent)

$b = \dfrac{3a}{4}$ ***AG***

**METHOD 2 (double-angle identity)**

$\dfrac{b}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{a}{\sin 2\theta}$

using double-angle identity ***(A1)***

$\dfrac{b}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{a}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}$ OR $b = \dfrac{a\sin\theta}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}$ OR $b = \dfrac{a}{2\cos\theta}$

correct working (involving substituting $\cos\theta = \dfrac{2}{3}$) that leads to ***AG*** ***A1***

$b = \dfrac{a\sin\theta}{2\sin\theta\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}$ OR $b = \dfrac{a\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)}{2\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}$ OR $b = \dfrac{a}{2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}$ (or equivalent)

$b = \dfrac{3a}{4}$ ***AG***

parts.label: c
parts.intro:
$[\text{BA}]$ is extended to form an isosceles triangle DAC, with $\hat{\text{D}} = \theta$, as shown in the following diagram.

![Line BAD with C above it: triangle ABC as before and triangle DAC with angle θ at D.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz2-q8b.png)
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1 (using supplementary angles)**

recognizing $\text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}$ and $\text{B}\hat{\text{A}}\text{C}$ are supplementary ***(M1)***

recognizing supplementary angles have the same sine value ***(A1)***

$\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D} = \sin 2\theta$

$\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}$ ***A1***

**METHOD 2 (using sine rule)**

recognizing $\text{CD} = a$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{a}{\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}} = \dfrac{b}{\sin\theta}$

correct substitution of $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ and $b = \dfrac{3a}{4}$ into sine rule ***(A1)***

$\dfrac{a}{\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}} = \dfrac{\left(\frac{3a}{4}\right)}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)}$ OR $\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D} = \dfrac{a\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)}{\left(\frac{3a}{4}\right)}$ (or equivalent)

$\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}$ ***A1***

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the area of triangle DAC, in terms of $a$.
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1 (using $\text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}$ in area formula)**

recognizing $\text{D}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A} = \theta$ ***(A1)***

recognizing $\text{AD} = b \ \left(= \dfrac{3a}{4}\right)$ ***(A1)***

correct substitution into area formula (must substitute expressions for two sides and name/expression/value for $\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}$) ***(M1)***

area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(b)(b)\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}\right)$ OR area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(b)(b)\sin 2\theta$ OR area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(b)(b)\sin \text{C}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D}$

correct substitution in terms of $a$ ***(A1)***

area $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{3a}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{3a}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{9}\right)$

area $= \dfrac{\sqrt{5}a^2}{8}$ ***A1***

**METHOD 2 (using $\text{A}\hat{\text{C}}\text{D}$ or $\text{A}\hat{\text{D}}\text{C}$ in area formula)**

recognizing $\text{CD} = a$ ***(A1)***

recognizing $\text{AD} = b \ \left(= \dfrac{3a}{4}\right)$ and/or $\text{D}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A} = \theta$ ***(A1)***

correct substitution into area formula (must substitute expressions for two sides and name/expression/value for $\sin \text{A}\hat{\text{D}}\text{C}$ or $\sin \text{A}\hat{\text{C}}\text{D}$) ***(M1)***

area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(a)(b)\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)$ OR area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(a)(b)\sin\theta$ OR area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(a)(b)\sin \text{A}\hat{\text{D}}\text{C}$ OR area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(a)(b)\sin \text{A}\hat{\text{C}}\text{D}$

correct substitution in terms of $a$ ***(A1)***

area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(a)\left(\dfrac{3a}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)$

area $= \dfrac{\sqrt{5}a^2}{8}$ ***A1***
